title: What stangent-bug-reproducer returns (Phase 3, D75, D76; v2: the truth map verdict, D361, D364)
description: A reproduction test it wrote, or why the bug can't be reproduced here. Code then builds and runs the test: it must fail on the named assertion, the quoted expected and actual results must be in the ticket word for word, and `shows` must be in the failure message (D95). A developer confirms the failure is the reported problem and a bug.

outcome.description: stopped (v2): no test, because the truth map contradicts the ticket or leaves it unclear (verdict).

target.description: The id of the test target the test was written in, as the input lists it.

testFile.description: The test file, relative to the repo root.

testName.description: The test's full name: Namespace.Class.Method for .NET; the full title for Jest, Vitest or Playwright.

line.description: The line in testFile where the assertion that checks the expected result starts.

expectedQuote.description: The ticket's sentence giving the expected result, word for word.

actualQuote.description: The ticket's sentence giving the actual result (what went wrong), word for word (D95).

shows.description: The words of your test's failure message that show that actual result, copied from the message (D95).

reason.description: For not-provable: why no unit or Playwright test can reach this behaviour here.

verdict.description: Only when the input has a truth map section: whether the PM's agreed rules back the ticket (D361). Code checks the entry and quote, and makes it unclear when the entry can't back a ticket.

entry.description: The truth entry it rests on (T1, T2, … from the input); required for backed and contradicted.

quote.description: Words from that entry (its FSD sentence, the PM's words, its section's text or the review's note), word for word.

why.description: In one or two sentences: how the entry backs, contradicts or leaves open what the ticket expects.
